chunks.label: Meals and food
chunks.rationale: Lets you talk about meals and ask about food and drink.
chunks.interference: Gohan, shokuji and meshi all mean meal; gohan is the default, shokuji more formal, meshi rough.

chunks.label: Water, tea and coffee
chunks.rationale: Lets you offer and ask for everyday hot and cold drinks.
chunks.interference: Omizu is cold or room-temperature water; hot water is always oyu.

chunks.label: Meat, fish and vegetables
chunks.rationale: Lets you say what you eat and shop for.

chunks.label: Jobs and days off
chunks.rationale: Lets you talk about your job, your pay and your time off.
chunks.interference: Yasumi is the day off itself; the verb to rest or take off is yasumu.

chunks.label: Breakfast basics
chunks.rationale: Lets you talk about breakfast and everyday groceries.
chunks.interference: Gyuunyuu is milk to drink; miruku is milk in coffee or for babies.

chunks.label: Beer, wine and juice
chunks.rationale: Lets you order or offer drinks at a meal or party.
chunks.interference: Juusu covers any sweet soft drink, not only fruit juice.

chunks.label: Sweets and snacks
chunks.rationale: Lets you talk about desserts, sweets and snacks.
chunks.interference: Okashi is the snack food itself; oyatsu is the snack between meals or snack time.

chunks.label: Popular dishes
chunks.rationale: Lets you name the dishes people go out for most.

chunks.label: School life
chunks.rationale: Lets you talk about your class, club, graduating and qualifications.
chunks.interference: Kurasu is your class group; a single lesson is jugyou.

chunks.label: Taste and seasoning
chunks.rationale: Lets you say how food tastes and what goes on it.
chunks.interference: Shio (salt) and shouyu (soy sauce) start with the same sound.

chunks.label: Home appliances
chunks.rationale: Lets you ask for and use the everyday machines at home.
chunks.interference: Renji is the microwave, never a stove or cooker.

chunks.label: Chores at home
chunks.rationale: Lets you talk about cooking, cleaning up and daily routines at home.
chunks.interference: Ryouri is any cooking; jisui is cooking your own meals instead of eating out.

chunks.label: Japanese home food
chunks.rationale: Lets you talk about everyday Japanese meals and packed lunches.
chunks.interference: Nabe is both the cooking pot and the hot-pot meal.

chunks.label: Eating out
chunks.rationale: Lets you handle restaurants, lunch out and takeaway.
chunks.interference: Gaishoku is the habit of eating out; ranchi is one lunch, usually out.

chunks.label: Teams and workplaces
chunks.rationale: Lets you talk about where you work and who you work with.
chunks.interference: Shokuba is any workplace, jimusho an office or agency, genba where the hands-on work happens.

chunks.label: Office tasks
chunks.rationale: Lets you talk about everyday office work.
chunks.interference: Shiryou are the prepared papers; deeta is the raw numbers or files.

drops.reason: Duplicate of 飯 (meshi), the same word written in kana.
